replication.target_description: Ahr et al. (2016), p.161 (PDF p.5), Prime: type-of-letter main effects on both accuracy and response time across first, third and fifth graders. Supplied locator and description do not distinguish these outcomes, so no unique target test can be assigned.

notes: Blind inputs 1601 and 1602 have identical descriptions, study and page locators; neither specifies which outcome. No assignment based on ID/input order. Located candidates at p.161, Prime: accuracy F(1,75)=10.75, p<.005, partial eta-squared=.13; RT F(1,75)=34.89, p<.001, partial eta-squared=.32. These are separate tests, not merged. p.160 Participants explicitly gives final n=78 children (31 first graders,22 third graders,25 fifth graders) after exclusion at chance performance; p.161 removes RT outliers beyond individual condition mean +/-2 SD. n fields left null under required failure-side convention because effect-level locator remains insufficient. Replication title verified against supplied reference; full-paper public HTML transcription cached at /home/lukas/.t3/worktrees/fred-data/audit-fred-stats-2026-10/audit/fred_stats_2026-10/texts/eb5d4130a63b419363f92754.txt. Author narrative replication verdict is common to all grade-specific negative-priming effects; it does not resolve the ambiguous statistic locator. Original acquisition failure recorded independently; replication paper is available. The explicit replication verdict concerns animal-probe negative priming; it is not applied to this ambiguous prime RT/accuracy target.
